messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details:  
The test `testRfc4648Section10Encode()` checks that encoding the string "f" produces the base64 output `"Zg=="`, as per RFC 4648 Section 10.

The reported bug is that `Base64.encodeBase64String()` is incorrectly chunking the output base64 string. The current implementation of `encodeBase64String` (lines 669-671) calls `encodeBase64(binaryData, true)`, where the `true` parameter indicates chunking enabled.

Looking at the `encodeBase64(byte[], boolean)` method (line 782), it delegates to `encodeBase64(byte[], boolean, boolean)` which defaults URL safety to false.

Further, the core `encodeBase64(byte[], boolean, boolean, int)` method (lines 820-835) creates a new `Base64` instance with a constructor either enabling or disabling chunking: when `isChunked` is true, it calls `new Base64(urlSafe)`, otherwise it calls `new Base64(0, CHUNK_SEPARATOR, urlSafe)`; the latter disables chunking by passing 0 for line length.

The `Base64(int, byte[], boolean)` constructor sets `this.lineLength` based on the lineLength parameter and disables chunking if lineLength is 0.

Finally, the `encode(byte[])` instance method performs the actual encoding using the configured chunk settings.

The root cause is that `encodeBase64String` passes `true` to enable chunking, but according to RFC 4648 Section 10 rules, the output base64 string should NOT be chunked (no intermediate line breaks). Thus, the test fails because `encodeBase64String("f".getBytes())` produces chunked base64 output instead of an unchunked string.

The bug report suggests changing `encodeBase64String` to call `encodeBase64(binaryData, false)` to disable chunking and produce a continuous base64 string without chunking / line breaks.

This will fix the failing test since `Base64.encodeBase64String()` will then produce the expected non-chunked RFC4648-compliant base64 output. The diagnosis aligns perfectly with the provided test and the bug report.

Summary: The failure occurs because `encodeBase64String` currently enables chunking due to the hardcoded `true` argument when calling `encodeBase64`. RFC4648 Section 10 requires base64 strings to be unchunked, so this argument should be changed to `false` to fix the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
